To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the potential energy surface in the self-consistently calculated fissioning systems has a complex structure that can not be described in a two-dimensional approach.

(i) a proper description of fission requires a multidimensional analysis of the energy surface, (ii) the energy landscape of heavy nuclei is complicated and can be described in terms of several minima, (iii) the choice of constraints is crucial for a correct description of the fission barriers and the fission path, and (iv) the use of the Gogney interaction is a promising approach for the study of fission of heavy nuclei.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the topography of multidimensional potential energy surfaces of heavy nuclei.
the multidimensional potential-energy surfaces in the self-consitent HFB approach.
the analysis of multidimensional energy surface and the description of fission barriers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multidimensional potential-energy surfaces should be used in order to describe fission correctly.
a multidimensional analysis of the potential energy surfaces is necessary to describe the fission process correctly.
a multidimensional potential energy landscape should be considered in order to fully describe fission barriers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to reproduce the main features of fission in the chosen nuclei.
the multidimensional potential-energy surface is not as smooth as it might seem from the two-dimensional analysis and the choice of the constraints is a crucial point in this type of studies.
the potential energy surface is a very complicated multidimensional function that requires a careful analysis of the constraints used in calculations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
one should be careful when analyzing the fission barrier height and shape, especially for heavy nuclei.
the choice of constraints on the quadrupole and hexadecapole moments is crucial in order to obtain a reasonable potential energy surface in the fissioning system.
the multidimensional calculations are necessary to obtain a complete picture of the fission process and to avoid misleading conclusions.
